title: Impulse waveform scratch: microburst warmup interplay
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal log exploring how short impulse-like request waves (10–50 reqs in <500ms) interact with warmup behavior, KV cache priming, and batching heuristics. Trying to capture reproducible signal and a couple of mitigation hypotheses to test in the next spike run.

Hypothesis summary (working):
- Small sharp impulses cause a short window where KV cache miss + cold kv-cache population + batcher coalescing delay combine to amplify p99 by 3–8x versus steady-state.
- If GPU scheduling/slotting introduces a 1x RTT to start, that compounds when the first few requests expect cached KV and penalties cascade (prefix not in cache -> longer decode -> later responses -> later cache population).
- Adaptive-batching that waits up to 12ms to coalesce can either help (more tokens per model invocation) or hurt (adds latency when impulse has only 1–2 requests). Need thresholding by recent-arrival-variance.

Experiment setup (env):
- Model: redwood-7b-quant (q4_0) on p4d-sim nodes (local perf rig)
- Runtime: feature-branch with impulse-log-timer enabled (PR #784)
- Requests: payload size ~ 80 tokens average, mean seq len 120 tokens, prompts deterministic (no tool-calls)
- Arrival pattern: baseline steady 120 qps for 60s, then impulse wave: 40ms-duration burst of 40 requests (Poisson within window), repeat every 30s for 10 cycles
- Metrics captured: per-request latency (start->first-byte and full-response), CPU/GPU util, KV-cache hit after request, batch size distribution, scheduling queues, thread preemption counts

Key config knobs toggled across runs:
- batch_timeout_ms = [3, 8, 12, 25]
- kv_cache_prefetch = [off, on-windowed(50ms), eager-on-first]  (eager-on-first attempts populate predicted prefixes immediately)
- request_priority = [uniform, burst-priority-low, burst-priority-high]
- prewarm_threshold = [0.0, 0.2]  (fraction of backend slots reserved for warmup)

Representative run notes (timestamps are relative to start of each impulse):
Run A (batch_timeout=3ms, kv_prefetch=off):
- p50 steady: 45ms, p95 steady: 90ms, p99 steady: 220ms
- Impulse cycle: p50 during impulse: 60ms, p95: 240ms, p99: 920ms (observed 4x jump vs steady p99)
- Batch size histogram: majority singletons during impulse (60%), small batch growth to 2–3 for tails
- KV hits: first 6 requests in impulse had 0 cache hit, hit rate ramps over 150ms
- Notes: scheduler queued many single-open calls -> GPU underutilized but high per-request latency due to startup overheads

Run B (batch_timeout=12ms, kv_prefetch=off):
- p50 steady: 50ms, p95 steady: 100ms, p99 steady: 240ms
- Impulse cycle: p50: 70ms, p95: 180ms, p99: 480ms (much improved over Run A)
- Batch size histogram: larger tail of 3–6 during impulse, some 10+ occasionally while waiting full 12ms
- KV hits: still cold for first bunch, but batched requests allowed amortization of model invocation cost
- Notes: batching saved token compute but added fixed wait; overall better p99 under this impulse profile

Run C (batch_timeout=8ms, kv_prefetch=eager-on-first):
- p50 steady: 48ms, p95 steady: 95ms, p99 steady: 230ms
- Impulse cycle: p50: 58ms, p95: 140ms, p99: 300ms
- KV hits: eager-on-first caused a 30–60ms warmup for predicted prefixes before user requests arrived -> first few requests more likely to hit
- Tradeoff: small steady-state overhead (~+6ms) but significant reduction in impulse p99

Run D (batch_timeout=8ms, kv_prefetch=on-windowed(50ms), request_priority=burst-priority-high):
- p99 impulse: 260ms, but noticed increased tail for background low-priority traffic (shifted to 1.1x p99)
- Observed fairness tradeoff: prioritizing bursts keeps interactive SLAs but moves tails to background lanes

Quick ASCII timeline (impulse snapshot):
0ms    20ms   40ms   60ms   80ms   100ms 
| reqs arrive -> batch collect -> model invoke -> decode -> cache write -> subsequent requests hit |
                                                     ^ cache ramp up usually completes ~120–200ms after first arrivals

Preliminary conclusions (working):
- For very short impulses (<=50 reqs, <=100ms window) increasing batch_timeout to ~8–12ms consistently reduces p99 versus minimal timeout, because it trades a few ms for substantial batching and model invocation amortization.
- KV-prefetch (eager-on-first) is promising: small steady cost but large reduction in cold-start impulse tails. However, correctness depends on accurate prefix predictions; mispredictions waste compute.
- Priority lanes are effective but must be coupled with global fairness SLOs: shifting tails to background customers is not acceptable without communicating degradation.
- A hybrid heuristic looks promising: if recent inter-arrival variance exceeds threshold X and burst size < Y then temporarily increase batch_timeout and enable one-shot eager-prefetch for common prefixes.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Measure real-world prefix predictability: how often is eager prefetch correct for our embed+tokenizer distribution (run against production prompt corpus sample)?
- Does prefetch + batching exacerbate memory pressure on smaller GPU instances? add memory-variance capture to next runs.
- Evaluate impact when model uses kv-cache heavy generation (long context streaming): does batch-amortization still dominate?

Planned follow-ups (short):
- Run the same impulse config against a larger model (redwood-13b-q4) to test model-size sensitivity (priority: medium).
- Add capture of per-invocation kernel times (compile + matmul + attention) to see where the 300–900ms tail is accumulating.
- Prototype hybrid heuristic in feature branch: detect impulse via sliding-window variance, bump timeout from 3ms->12ms for next 150ms and trigger a single eager-prefetch for top-3 prefixes.

Notes-to-self: keep these quick runs reproducible: commit PR/branch tag and attach run sha to the confluence notes. When writing up, include a small demo script to reproduce arrival waveform (ramp+impulse).

Rough action items:
- [ ] Push perf-run tooling to emit kernel-level timestamps (Mateo)
- [ ] Run prefix-predict audit on 7 days of anonymized prompts (Sofia)
- [ ] Prototype hybrid-batcher heuristic and gate behind feature flag (Elina)
- [ ] Add fairness telemetry to track p99s by customer lane and diff pre/post heuristic

Random observations:
- Cold KV population often has an initial hysteresis: first invocations are long but subsequent ones for same prefix drop quickly — suggests prewarming single representative request per prefix is high ROI.
- When impulse frequency increases (cycles <10s apart) the system effectively stays warm and tail disappears — so goal is to shorten that warm-up window rather than fully avoid initial cost.

End of scratch.
